Comprehension Passage – II (Questions 46 – 50): Read the following passage carefully and

Biomimicry—the discipline of emulating nature's time-tested forms, processes, and ecosystems to
solve human engineering challenges—is quietly reshaping sustainable design. Rather than
conquering nature through brute energy consumption, biomimetic engineers study how organisms
achieve extraordinary structural efficiency with minimal material waste. For instance, the
aerodynamic nose cone of Japan's Shinkansen bullet train was modelled on the beak of the
kingfisher to eliminate sonic booms when exiting tunnels, simultaneously reducing electricity
consumption by fifteen percent. Similarly, architects have designed passive cooling systems for
high-rise buildings inspired by the self-regulating ventilation chimneys of African termite mounds.
By treating the natural world as a mentor rather than a mere warehouse of raw materials,
biomimicry fosters innovations that are inherently regenerative.
